evidence: SB 6 (2025) and the PUCT's large-load interconnection standards for loads of 75 MW or more in ERCOT (Project 58481) were adopted in Sept 2026, and PUCT approved the ERCOT Batch Zero framework on June 18, 2026; this is a mandated interconnection/cost framework for all ERCOT utilities rather than a classic rate class.

evidence: ERCOT large loads must post financial security (proposed at $50,000 per MW) plus pay 100% of direct interconnection costs; Batch Zero applies a $50,000/MW default security and CIAC payments; the final rule dropped the non-refundable fee and 80% forfeiture but retained security.

ERCOT tracks more than 438,000 MW of large-load requests; Batch Zero results and MW allocations are not due until April 9, 2027 with a final transmission plan in fall 2027, and the TCEQ pause adds further delay.
Sales tax exemption on data center equipment and electricity requires at least $200M investment, 100,000 sq ft and 20 permanent jobs, with self-certification and repayment if requirements fail.
pending: Senate Finance chair says the Legislature will revisit it next session; Abbott wants incentives eliminated.

evidence: Exemption carries job and investment conditions and projects that fail must repay avoided tax; of 20 projects audited, six were noncompliant or withdrew, but verification lags for years.

evidence: Texas Water Code requires data centers and other major users to return the annual TWDB water-use survey (failure is a criminal offense and blocks TCEQ permits); Abbott ordered enforcement Sept 14, 2026 and the AG opened an investigation Sept 24, 2026.

evidence: SB 6 allows curtailment of new transmission-level large loads (connected after Dec 31, 2025) in load shed and lets ERCOT require loads with backup generation covering 50%+ of demand to deploy it or curtail before or during an energy emergency.
